name: Artemis II
summary: An interactive Artemis II mission experience built in Swift and SceneKit.
description: A playable, scientifically-grounded walkthrough of NASA's Artemis II lunar flyby, built entirely in Swift and SceneKit with no external 3D assets. Selected as one of 350 winners of Apple's Swift Student Challenge 2026 — which meant three days at Apple Park for WWDC '26.
highlights: Orbital mechanics simulated and rendered in real time
Every 3D asset generated procedurally in SceneKit
Selected from tens of thousands of global submissions

name: CRIS.ai
summary: A real-time AI crisis response system.
description: A voice-first emergency triage system that listens to a caller, classifies the nature and severity of the crisis in real time, and routes it to the right responder — built in 24 hours and taking first place in the ElevenLabs track at Hack4Humanity 2026.
highlights: Sub-second speech-to-intent classification
Severity-aware routing to the correct responder
Won the ElevenLabs track against 38 submissions

name: WC26 Intelligence
summary: An ML platform predicting international football and simulating the 2026 World Cup.
description: A hobby machine-learning platform that models international football using gradient-boosted trees, Bayesian hierarchical models, graph neural networks and stacked ensembles, then runs Monte Carlo simulations over the full 2026 World Cup bracket. It called Spain over Argentina in the final.
highlights: Correctly predicted Spain over Argentina in the final
Stacked ensemble over trees, Bayesian and graph models
Full-tournament Monte Carlo bracket simulation

name: Mean Reversion Backtester
summary: A research engine exploring mean reversion, risk, and market regimes.
description: A backtesting engine for systematically testing whether a mean-reversion edge actually exists — with regime detection, risk decomposition, and the kind of honest statistics that usually kill a strategy before it reaches capital.
highlights: Regime-aware evaluation instead of a single blended backtest
Risk and drawdown decomposition per market regime
Built to disprove strategies, not flatter them

name: Vibe Trading
summary: An agentic trading assistant that reasons about markets in natural language.
description: A personal trading agent that turns a plain-language thesis into a testable strategy — pulling data, forming a position view, and explaining its reasoning rather than emitting an opaque signal.
highlights: Natural-language thesis to executable strategy
Explains its reasoning instead of emitting a black-box signal

name: Hackmarket
summary: A two-sided marketplace for AI tools, with a managed API gateway.
description: Sellers upload AI/API tools; buyers call them through a managed gateway that handles auth, routing, usage metering, billing, demos and seller analytics — so neither side has to build the boring half of an API business.
highlights: Managed gateway handling auth, routing and metering
Usage-based billing with seller-side analytics

name: Homeability.ai
summary: Accessibility scoring for housing, built in 22 hours.
description: A system that scores homes and neighbourhoods for accessibility — placing 3rd overall in the "AI for Scalable Solutions" track at the AWS × INRIX Hackathon, against 254 participants and 38 submissions.
highlights: 3rd of 38 submissions, 254 participants
Built in a 22-hour hackathon window

name: Live Character Lamp Robot
summary: A Luxo-style desk lamp with a personality, simulated in 5 degrees of freedom.
description: An expressive character driven by a simulated 5-DOF lamp robot — the Pixar lamp problem taken seriously, where personality has to emerge from joint angles and timing alone, with no face and no voice.
highlights: Personality expressed purely through 5-DOF motion
Real-time inverse kinematics in the browser

name: Hiring Agent
summary: An agent that evaluates and scores resumes.
description: An LLM agent that reads a resume against a role and produces a structured, defensible score — built to surface the reasoning behind a rating rather than hide it behind a number.
highlights: Structured, explainable scoring rubric

name: fastASL
summary: Real-time sign language translation, pronounced "fast as hell".
description: A translation pipeline between American Sign Language and text, optimised for latency — because a translator that lags is a translator nobody uses.
highlights: Latency-first architecture for live conversation

name: Unit Test Generator
summary: LLM-driven Google Test generation for C++ projects.
description: Generates, refines and repairs Google Test unit tests for arbitrary C++ projects using local LLMs via Ollama, iterating against compiler output and coverage until the tests actually build and pass.
highlights: Iterates against real compiler errors until tests compile
Coverage-guided refinement loop

name: Synapse
summary: A habit tracker that grows a brain out of your habits.
description: Every habit completion spawns a glowing neuron inside a translucent brain; consecutive-day streaks wire synapses between them. Five life categories map to distinct anatomical regions, so over months your habits physically reshape the brain on screen.
highlights: Hebbian growth model — cells that fire together, wire together
Brain geometry extruded procedurally from Bézier paths
Time-lapse scrubber over months of completion data
